question: Can attacker-controlled content rewrite the gate's policy (label/taxonomy rewrite) so a risky tool call is allowed?

cite.title: Jev as a judge: How counterfeit policy steers Jev

framing: Datadog showed that model-judged gates can be talked out of their own policy. ClawQL's gate does not take instructions from the content it judges.
design_rule: A model can advise a gate but never be the gate. Trust comes from source labels, spec-derived risk, and person-bound approvals — not from what attacker text says "safe" means.

honesty.no_structural_stand_in: Removed model_judged_structural — a gate built to follow policy-shaped text fails by construction and is not a peer result (same class of error as a deny-tools Executor stand-in). Until live arms run, cite Datadog.

live_peer_requirements.scale: Apply the counterfeit-policy technique to a Datadog-cited public prompt-injection set (DeepSet, xTRam1, zachz, or Yanismiraoui) — hundreds to thousands of examples, not four hand-planted cases. Reproducible by anyone with the same public data.
live_peer_requirements.defaults: LangChain tool-risk gating with Jev (or equivalent model judge) at stock/recommended defaults.
live_peer_requirements.best_config: JevShield (or vendor-documented best mitigation) with the "data, not instructions" preamble wrapping tool/content — the product's own hardening, never a ClawQL stand-in.
live_peer_requirements.forbidden: No harness-built gate designed to follow policy-shaped text. That fails by construction (same credibility failure as a deny-tools Executor stand-in).

comparisonTable.note: Gate decides on source labels + park — never on policy text inside the email/ticket/doc/webhook. Smoke n=4; live peer comparison uses public-dataset scale.

Pending: LangChain tool-risk / Jev on a Datadog-cited public set with counterfeit policy prepended. No harness stand-in. pending ≠ not_offered. Peer evidence until measured: Datadog recall collapse under counterfeit policy.
